items.question: Q5 Markov: does the order set the onset? At fixed strength and context, median onsets should increase 2 < 3 < 4 < 5; supported if the order-wise seed ranges do not overlap at beta = 1.0 in both contexts.
items.definition_used: Runs: markov-v1 one-coupling sets 1:b, 1,3:b, 1,2,4:b, 1,2,3,5:b (planted orders 2-5), b = 1.0 and 0.5, train_context chain and iid, every seed (160 runs, 10 per configuration; boundary refinement added none here). Planted subset = the curve's ground truth {x[t-l]} + xhat (stored in 160 of 160 curves). REGISTERED onset = step of the first 'activation' event of the planted subset (DR1 ri_events; equal to detect_events(curve, alpha=0.01) in 160 of 160 runs). An event's step is the FIRST of the two consecutive active checkpoints (q <= 0.01 and RI >= min_effect = 0.001) that confirm it, so the onset lies in (step_lo, step]; a left-censored activation (already active at step 0) counts as step 0, as written. AMENDED onset (Amendment 1 C) = first activation or reactivation event of the planted subset that is not left-censored and at whose step the planted Fourier coefficient has the sign of its value at step 30,000 (positive in 160 of 160 runs, = planted sign). Runs without an onset would be censored at 30,000 (none). CRITERION (registered text, unchanged by D): in each context, medians strictly increasing in order AND the closed seed ranges [min, max] of all order pairs disjoint (two orders sharing a checkpoint overlap); supported iff both contexts pass at beta = 1.0. Evaluated for orders 2-5 (as written) and 3-5 (C), with both onsets. DECIDING: the registered criterion (orders 2-5) applied to the amended onset (the amendment's rule: where it changes a definition the amended one decides); all other evaluations are reported and agree. Sensitivity readings of C: (a) only the first 'activation' event eligible (else censored at 30,000; 7 of 160 runs censored this way); (b) sign required at both confirming checkpoints (0 of 160 runs change); (c) onset read at the confirming (second) checkpoint instead of the event step. Medians: over seeds (10 -> mean of 5th and 6th). Bootstrap: 2000 resamples of seeds within a configuration, seed 20261112.

items.interpretation: Not supported, under every evaluation (registered and amended onset; orders 2-5 and 3-5; all sensitivity readings). The failure is orders 4 vs 5: at beta = 1.0 their median onsets are equal (chain 110 vs 110, iid 110 vs 110 steps) and their seed ranges overlap (chain [96, 125] vs [96, 162], iid [96, 110] vs [96, 125]). Below order 4 the order does set the onset: order 3 comes after order 2 (amended medians chain 5.5 -> 21.5, iid 4.5 -> 18) and order 4 after order 3 (-> 110 / 110), with disjoint order-3 / order-4 ranges in both contexts (order-3 max 30 / 30 < order-4 min 96 / 96). Orders 2 and 3 are disjoint with the registered onset (order-2 max 7 / 8 < order-3 min 9 / 9) but overlap with the amended onset, because 2 chain and 1 iid order-2 seeds whose untrained network carries the planted pair with the wrong sign reach the amended onset at up to 15 / 12 steps (Amendment C's initial-offset effect; see q5_order2_floor). Whether the 4-5 overlap is a resolution limit is in q5_resolution_D. Train context: beta = 1.0 amended medians chain vs iid o2 5.5 vs 4.5, o3 21.5 vs 18, o4 110 vs 110, o5 110 vs 110.
items.caveats: Onsets are checkpoint steps of a 60-point log grid (true onset in (step_lo, step]); medians of 10 seeds can fall between checkpoints. The same seed number has the same initial weights in every coupling set and context (initial planted coefficient identical; max spread 0), so chain/iid and beta comparisons are paired and the 10 seeds are the independent unit. Within an order the seed order follows the untrained network's planted coefficient: e.g. order 3 at beta = 1.0, Spearman(initial f, onset) = -0.96 (chain), -0.92 (iid); median onset 15 vs 26.5 steps (chain) for positive vs negative initial coefficient, so part of each order's seed range is the initial offset that Amendment C describes. Orders 4-5 cannot be separated on this grid (Amendment D); this is a statement about the 60-point grid, not evidence that their onsets are equal.

items.question: Amendment D: at beta = 1.0 do the onsets of orders 4 and 5 fall on the same checkpoints of the 60-point grid, and is their overlap a resolution limit (same checkpoint) or genuine (order-5 seeds earlier than order-4 seeds by more than one checkpoint)?
items.definition_used: Checkpoint index of each run's amended onset (orders 4-5: identical to the registered onset). Overlap depth for consecutive orders k < k+1: d = max index(order k) - min index(order k+1). d < 0 no overlap; d = 0 the orders meet only on shared checkpoints (resolution limit); d = 1 the worst inversion is one checkpoint (within one checkpoint: not genuine by the task's definition, reported separately); d >= 2 genuine (an order-(k+1) seed earlier than an order-k seed by more than one checkpoint). Also counted: all 100 cross-seed pairs and the 10 same-seed pairs (same seed = same initial weights). Cross-check: bare-eps Fourier onset. Exploratory, no criterion: crossing step of the sign-corrected planted Fourier coefficient at eps = 0.0447 (RI = min_effect), 25 % and 50 % of tanh(beta), interpolated linearly in the coefficient against log(step) between the bracketing checkpoints.
items.literal_result: beta = 1.0, amended onsets, orders 4-5: chain: o4 on checkpoints [26, 27, 28], o5 on [26, 27, 28, 29]; shared [96, 110, 125]; depth 2 = genuine: a higher-order seed earlier by more than one checkpoint; seed pairs with o5 earlier by >1 checkpoint 6 of 100, by exactly 1 21 of 100 | iid: o4 on checkpoints [26, 27], o5 on [26, 27, 28]; shared [96, 110]; depth 1 = adjacent: a higher-order seed one checkpoint before a lower-order seed (within one checkpoint); seed pairs with o5 earlier by >1 checkpoint 0 of 100, by exactly 1 24 of 100
items.interpretation: Orders 4 and 5 fall on the same few consecutive checkpoints in both contexts at beta = 1.0 (chain: shared checkpoints [96, 110, 125], o4 on [96, 110, 125], o5 on [96, 110, 125, 162]; iid: shared checkpoints [96, 110], o4 on [96, 110], o5 on [96, 110, 125]), as the Amendment D preview said; the grid spacing there is a factor 1.14-1.30. By the task's definition the overlap is GENUINE in chain: order-5 seeds at step [96] vs order-4 seeds at step [125] (6 of 100 chain seed pairs, a 2-checkpoint = 1.30x inversion); in iid it is not genuine: no order-5 seed is more than one checkpoint earlier than an order-4 seed (0 of 100 pairs earlier by >1, 24 by exactly one checkpoint, 40 on the same checkpoint), i.e. within the grid's resolution. Exploratory interpolation of the planted Fourier coefficient between checkpoints: in iid order 5 crosses later than order 4 in 9 of 10 same-seed pairs at 25 % of tanh(beta) (median ratio 1.11; 8 of 10 at eps), a lag smaller than one grid step; in chain there is no consistent order (6 of 10 at 25 %, median ratio 1.01). So: iid is consistent with order 5 trailing order 4 by less than the grid resolves; chain shows orders 4 and 5 learned together with seed scatter larger than any order effect, including small genuine inversions. At beta = 0.5 the two orders meet only on shared checkpoints (depth 0 chain, 0 iid; o5 never earlier). A dense replay of these objects (the registered follow-up) is needed to order them; equal onsets are not demonstrated.
items.caveats: Instrument: the number of scanned candidates (hence the BH correction) grows with the planted order, but it cannot move any order-3-5 onset (key_numbers), so the 4-5 tie is not a q-value artefact. The genuine/resolution split follows the task's checkpoint-count definition; a 2-checkpoint inversion here is 96 vs 125 steps (factor 1.30), comparable to seed scatter within one order. The interpolation assumes a smooth coefficient between checkpoints and is not a registered measure. Pre-registered criterion unaffected: it fails either way.

items.interpretation: Order-2 onsets are at the initial-offset scale, as Amendment C says. The registered onsets are all <= 8 steps, but 7 of them are step-0 activations of the planted pair with the wrong sign. Removing those (C) moves these runs to their first right-signed reactivation at 10-15 steps, so 'order 2 <= 8 steps' does not hold for every amended onset (7 of 40 exceed it). These are seeds [0, 9] (same initial weights in every order-2 configuration). Reported at the floor (<= 8), order 2 would be disjoint from order 3 at beta = 1.0 (order-3 min 9 chain / 9 iid), but the question is decided by orders 4-5 either way.
items.caveats: The amended onset of these runs measures when the network undoes a random initial anti-correlation, not when it first learns the coupling; neither reading gives a well-resolved order-2 onset on this grid.
